c.tagline: Altbier, avant-garde art, and the longest bar in the world.

taxi.fareNote: Metered; hail at ranks or book via the FreeNow app

emergency.note: EU emergency 112 reaches police, fire and ambulance

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the Altstadt bar strip at night, and the area around the Hauptbahnhof and Worringer Platz can feel seedy after dark.

hood_desc: The compact medieval old town on the Rhine, nicknamed 'the longest bar in the world' for the 300-odd pubs, breweries and restaurants packed into half a square kilometre; the place to drink Altbier and go out, lively and loud after dark.

Düsseldorf's glossy heart along the tree-lined 'Kö' boulevard and its canal, with flagship designer boutiques, department stores and grand cafes; central, walkable and the natural base for shopping and sightseeing.
A former harbour reborn as a design and media district, with Frank Gehry's tilting Neuer Zollhof towers, waterfront restaurants, rooftop bars and clubs; stylish and best experienced in the evening.
The city's creative, bohemian quarter of street art, vintage shops, third-wave coffee and indie bars along Ackerstraße; popular with a younger, arty crowd.

A leafy, affluent residential district across the Rhine, full of Art Nouveau villas, quiet streets and river views back to the old-town skyline; calm and family-friendly, a short tram ride from the centre.
lodging: Radisson Blu Media Harbour Hotel Düsseldorf

water.note: Tap water is high quality and safe to drink.

transit.hours: U-Bahn, trams and S-Bahn run roughly 4:30am-1am, with all-night service on Friday and Saturday nights and NachtExpress night buses filling the gaps midweek.
transit.pay: Buy tickets from the Rheinbahn app, station machines or on trams/buses; a single EinzelTicket (price level A) costs about 3.40 EUR (~US$3.70) and a 24-hour ticket about 7.90 EUR, covering VRR U-Bahn, trams, buses and S-Bahn across the region. Staying weeks? The Deutschland-Ticket (63 EUR/month) covers all local transit nationwide.

transit.m: SkyTrain to Düsseldorf Flughafen station, then regional train

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving ~5-10% for good service is customary — tell the server the total when you pay.

food.name: Rheinischer Sauerbraten
food.desc: Beef marinated for days in vinegar and wine, braised, then served in a dark sweet-sour gravy thickened with gingerbread, with red cabbage and dumplings.

places.name: Zum Schiffchen
places.note: Trading since 1628 and claimed as the city's oldest restaurant; Napoleon ate here.

places.name: Brauerei Schumacher
places.note: Family brewery restaurant since 1838, the benchmark for Rhineland home cooking.

places.name: Brauerei im Fuchschen
places.note: Loud, wood-panelled brewhouse doing the full traditional plate with its own Alt.

food.name: Halve Hahn
food.desc: Not half a chicken at all: a dark rye roll with a thick slab of aged Gouda, butter, mustard, onion rings and paprika. The classic thing to eat with Alt.

places.name: Zum Uerige
places.note: The most famous Alt brewhouse; Halve Hahn and Blutwurst at the standing barrels.

places.name: Brauerei im Fuchschen
places.note: Cheap, correct version to soak up a few Alt on the copper-topped tables.

places.name: Zum Schlussel
places.note: Brewhouse in the heart of the Altstadt; good if Uerige is three deep at the bar.

food.name: Senfrostbraten
food.desc: Steak crusted with the city's sharp ABB mustard and topped with fried onions. Duesseldorf mustard is stronger and far less sweet than the Bavarian kind.

places.name: Zum Uerige
places.note: Mustard-crusted roast beef from the brewhouse kitchen, best with a fresh Alt.

places.name: Brauerei Schumacher
places.note: Old-school preparation with fried onions and bratkartoffeln.

places.name: Zum Schiffchen
places.note: Historic dining rooms and a full roster of Rhenish meat classics.

food.name: Himmel un Aad
food.desc: Heaven and earth: fried blood sausage with mashed potato, apple sauce and a heap of browned onions. The most Rhenish plate on any Altstadt menu.

places.name: Brauerei im Fuchschen
places.note: Serves the dish year round; the blood sausage comes crisp at the edges.

places.name: Zum Schlussel
places.note: Reliable version in a busy brewhouse with its own unfiltered Alt.

places.name: Zum Uerige
places.note: Order it at the wooden counter with a Blutwurst roll on the side.

food.name: Reibekuchen
food.desc: Grated potato pancakes fried hard and eaten hot with apple sauce or dark beet syrup. Sold from stalls, and unmissable at the Christmas markets.

places.name: Carlsplatz Markt
places.note: Daily covered market with a reibekuchen stand plus cheese, fish and wine bars.

places.name: Brauerei im Fuchschen
places.note: Kitchen version served with apple sauce if the market stalls are shut.

places.name: Altstadt Christmas markets
places.note: From late November the stalls fry them nonstop; best eaten standing in the cold.

food.name: Krustchen
food.desc: A Rhineland pub staple: breaded pork schnitzel on a slice of dark rye bread with a fried egg on top and fried potatoes alongside. Unfussy and filling.

places.name: Zum Schlussel
places.note: Textbook Krustchen with the egg cooked to order and its own Alt to wash it down.

places.name: Brauerei Schumacher
places.note: Generous portions in the brewery's old dining room, popular at lunch.

places.name: Brauerei im Fuchschen
places.note: Good-value plate in the loudest, most cheerful of the Altstadt brewhouses.

food.name: Altbier
food.desc: Copper-coloured top-fermented beer served in small straight 0.2 litre glasses. Waiters keep replacing them until you put your beer mat on the glass.

places.name: Zum Uerige
places.note: The definitive Alt, poured straight from wooden casks by famously brusque waiters.

places.name: Brauerei Schumacher
places.note: Oldest surviving Alt brewery in the city, brewing on site since 1838.

places.name: Brauerei im Fuchschen
places.note: Maltier house Alt and a legendary Christmas bock; standing room only at peak.

food.name: Killepitsch
food.desc: Blood-red herbal liqueur made in the Altstadt from around ninety herbs and berries, drunk ice cold as a shot after beer. Invented here in the 1950s.

places.name: Et Kabuffke
places.note: The tiny hatch bar where Killepitsch is made and sold; the original address.

places.name: Bolkerstrasse bars
places.note: Almost every bar on the longest bar in the world pours it by the shot.

places.name: Zum Schlussel
places.note: Convenient nightcap after Alt and a plate of Rhenish food.

landmarks: Rheinturm
This 240-meter telecommunications tower with a distinctive light-based clock display dominates the Düsseldorf skyline.
Königsallee
Düsseldorf's grand boulevard, lined with a central canal, chestnut trees, and luxury boutiques, is the city's most photographed street.
Medienhafen (Media Harbour)
A former industrial harbor transformed into a striking architectural showcase, including Frank Gehry's wave-like Neuer Zollhof buildings.
Schlossturm
This lone surviving tower of Düsseldorf's medieval castle stands at the Rhine promenade as a picturesque link to the city's past.
Schloss Benrath
An elegant pink 18th-century pleasure palace surrounded by symmetrical gardens and reflecting ponds, a masterpiece of Rococo design.
Kö-Bogen
A striking modern architectural complex with green, undulating facades by Daniel Libeskind at the head of the Königsallee.
Altstadt (Old Town)
Known as the 'longest bar in the world,' this historic old town is packed with narrow lanes, breweries, and lively photogenic charm.
Basilika St. Lambertus
This Gothic basilica with its distinctive twisted spire is a historic landmark overlooking the Rhine in the Altstadt.
Rheinkniebrücke
An elegant cable-stayed bridge over the Rhine, especially striking when illuminated at dusk against the city skyline.
Hofgarten
Düsseldorf's oldest and largest public park, offering leafy paths, monuments, and a green escape in the heart of the city.

train.note: Long-distance trains use Dusseldorf Hauptbahnhof, but many ICE, IC and Eurostar services also call at Dusseldorf Flughafen Fernbahnhof, which is very handy if you are flying in or out. Cologne is 25 minutes by ICE, Amsterdam about 2h15 and Brussels around 2h30. Eurostar fares on the Brussels and Paris route are yield-managed, open roughly six months ahead and are not interchangeable with DB tickets on the same trains, so book early and check both. The OeBB Nightjet from Amsterdam to Vienna and Innsbruck calls here in the evening.

intl.to: Amsterdam, Brussels, Paris, Prague & across Europe

bus.note: The main long-distance coach stop is on the Worringer Strasse side of Dusseldorf Hauptbahnhof rather than a dedicated terminal, and some services also call at the airport. FlixBus is the dominant operator and tickets are bought online. Amsterdam takes about 3h30 by coach, Brussels around 4h and Cologne 45 minutes, so the coach is mostly a budget alternative rather than a time saver.

intl.to: Cologne, Zons & the Lower Rhine (Germany) - sails from the Altstadt landing stages at the Burgplatz / Rathausufer

ferry.note: There is no sea ferry from Dusseldorf - it is an inland Rhine port about 200 km from the coast. KD runs panorama cruises and day trips from the Altstadt quay by the Burgplatz, including sailings downriver to Zons and up to Cologne, mostly between spring and autumn plus Advent cruises. River-cruise vessels also dock along the Rheinufer promenade, and small local ferries cross the Rhine north of the city.

half.name: Cologne
half.blurb: Rhine city dominated by its twin-spired Gothic cathedral, with a lively old town of breweries along the riverbank.

half.name: Xanten Archaeological Park
half.blurb: Reconstructed Roman city on the site of Colonia Ulpia Traiana, with rebuilt amphitheater, baths, and city walls.

half.name: Aachen
half.blurb: Charlemagne's former capital near the Belgian and Dutch borders, centered on its octagonal Carolingian cathedral.
